answers.text: "A fresh new high in a rising weekly is the buy." A new high is criterion 7 only. The Template is all eight or none (C3): rs_rank_pct 69.65 fails criterion 8, and W mixed (not HH/HL) with flat ma100/ma200 does not confirm stage 2 (C2). The grid adds nothing my test fails on; I hold.

"Stage label by MA slope is not my test." It is mine: the MA stack and RS are criteria 1-4 and 8 (C3). D HH/HL at dist_to_20bar_high_pct 0.24 shows the break, but rs_rank_pct 69.65 under 70 still fails the gate. A value-area break is not evidence my method weighs; I hold.

"Not a breakout bar: elder drops 10 to 7." Elder is advisory on my card. The breakout already printed on day_vol 2.72; the D red bar 2.5% under the 20-day high is the first pullback my case waits for (C5). W HH/HL, 9>21 keeps stage 2. Volume on the pullback decides (C6), not the impulse tick.

"A base under the pivot is no buy signal." Agreed, and my claim never said buy now: the buy is the pivot clear on volume (C5). Strength stands (rs_rank_pct 96.39); W 13.2% under the 20-wk high is inside criterion 7's 25%. D RANGE, red bar is the quiet right side of the base I want.

"'Near highs' is 6.0% under the 20-day high." Criterion 7 asks within 25%; 6.0% passes. The point I accept is timing: D RANGE with no pivot break means no buy yet (C5), which is why I wait for a tight pause and a new closing high. The claim itself stands on the Template.
